findings.claim: Immediate selection evidence and descendant credit disagree in kind, not just magnitude. Endpoint (last-record) contrasts are large and coherent for pair_kernel_1.5/2.5 (endpoint_effects:9,10; positive_batch_fraction 1.0) and landmark_00_occupancy3 (endpoint_effects:15), whereas survival credit for the same landmark_00_soft_mass is weak (survival_effects:0, effect_z 0.365, q 0.12) and its change-rate is null (survival_effects:200). Because decoded_terminal_learning_labels_available is false, last-record joint-head credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit; the immediate-vs-descendant comparison is unavailable and direction priorities should not be set from survival credit alone.

Ancestral coverage is thin: lineage_support reports 349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 with fewer than 6, out of 700 batch nodes, and only 14 complete-survival batches. Survival fields are BH-adjusted jointly over 400 tests and are explicitly not terminal affinity effects. Survivor bias is therefore expected, and the recorded joint-head credit is a selection/survival proxy rather than a decoded terminal label.

Ranking by point estimate alone would over-prioritize the largest-magnitude endpoint effects. Multiplicity-adjusted support and independent-batch agreement favor the short-range pair kernels: pair_kernel_1.5 and 2.5 have q ~1.5e-4 and 2.2e-5 with positive_batch_fraction 1.0 (endpoint_effects:9,10), and their branch-adjusted covariance/correlation entries are among the few surviving q<0.05 with same_sign_batch_fraction ~0.79-0.93 (branch_adjusted:86,87,240,241). pair_kernel_7.0 has a comparable point magnitude but negative direction and zero positive batches (endpoint_effects:13), so a point-estimate ranking would mis-order it.

Joint pose/shape diagnostics carry the strongest and most reproducible branch-adjusted signals: joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_internal_RMS_A are negative with q ~1e-4 to 3e-2 and same_sign_batch_fraction 0.79-1.0 across raw and adjusted covariance/correlation (branch_adjusted:74,76,151,153,228,230,305,307). These are joint (global-plus-internal) quantities, so they indicate that a region's information is not separable from common motion; the supplied tool performed the adjustment, and no claim is made beyond it.

Global centroid coordinates do not survive adjustment: raw_covariance centroid entries have q 0.69-0.97 (branch_adjusted:0,1,2) and adjusted_covariance/adjusted_correlation centroid entries remain null (branch_adjusted:77,78,79,231,232,233). This is the concrete case where the adjusted ranking differs from the raw point-estimate ranking, and it argues against prioritizing global translation as a coordinate rule.

Shape_yy is the one shape component with a consistent negative sign across raw and adjusted correlation (branch_adjusted:158,235; q 4e-5 and 3e-4, same_sign_batch_fraction 1.0), while shape_xx and shape_zz are weaker and less consistent (branch_adjusted:4,81,5,82). The counterexample that would weaken a shape_yy direction is a batch with opposite sign; the supplied same_sign_batch_fraction of 1.0 means no such batch is present in the 14 independent batches, so the direction is reproducible within the supplied evidence.

The supplied continuous contrast functions for landmark_00 span the full observed support [0.0,0.49] with many sign changes (e.g. 4-10 sign changes per feature) and strong_sign_conflicts up to 14, and polynomial fits are rejected (polynomial_accepted false) with relative_node_RMSE 0.29-0.87. A constant rule is therefore not supported by these curves; only observed-node interpolation within the window is defensible, and no extrapolation or arbitrary time binning is permitted.

Soft-mass curves for landmarks 00-09 show sign changes and rate reversals within the window (first_rate_z and last_rate_z of opposite sign for several landmarks), so a time-conditioned rule would differ from a constant rule. However, the curves are contrasts, not absolute reward targets, and the fits are not validated as causal; the evidence supports only a descriptive time-conditioned contrast, not a reward target.

Turnover accounting separates within-path change from cohort composition: for landmark_00_soft_mass the population rate is null (turnover:0) while edge_rate and turnover_residual_rate are both significant with opposite signs (turnover:1,2), and the same pattern appears for landmark_00_local_cxx/cyy (turnover:14,17) and landmark_07_local_cxx/cyy (turnover:224,227). The residual is an accounting diagnostic that includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not a causal selection effect or atom velocity, so it cannot by itself establish within-path change.

Parent-child increment contrasts are mostly null or marginal: landmark_00_softmin has a negative integrated rate (increment_effects:14, q 0.046) and landmark_00_occupancy3 a positive one (increment_effects:15, q 0.081), while shape_xx and shape_yy are negative with q 0.095 and 0.16 (increment_effects:3,4). These are weaker than the corresponding endpoint effects, so the evidence does not support treating increment contrasts as the primary direction signal.

Joint diagnostics show that selection innovation is positively associated with native alignment and teacher innovation-contrast alignment (joint_diagnostics:1,11; p ~1e-9, positive_batch_fraction 1.0) but negatively associated with observed child score gain (joint_diagnostics:2; p 1.8e-7, positive_batch_fraction 0.0). Teacher contrast is predominantly internal (joint_diagnostics:14, mean 0.79) with atom participation 0.38 (joint_diagnostics:15), so coherent joint patterns, not isolated marginal descriptors, carry the reproducible coupling.

The information audit reports compressed-choice excess fixed-RMS of 0.081 A (CI 0.070-0.092) and top4 teacher overlap 0.470 (CI 0.427-0.515), with the explicit limitation that these are not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian and that teacher score correlations are observational. Curve_support selects 24 features under a fidelity rule but marks legendre_runtime_allowed false for all listed features. These diagnostics bound what can be claimed: they support descriptive coordinate contrasts, not a causal affinity gradient.

hypotheses.claim: A short-range pair-distance shell (pair_kernel_1.5-2.5) is the most reproducible coordinate contrast in the supplied evidence, with consistent sign across endpoint, branch-adjusted covariance and branch-adjusted correlation. A discriminating failure condition would be a batch with opposite sign or a null adjusted q; neither is present in the 14 supplied batches.

Joint innovation and internal RMS are the strongest joint diagnostics and are negatively signed with high batch agreement. A testable coordinate intervention would target the joint internal RMS while retaining freedom in the surrounding landmark coordinates; the failure condition is a batch where the adjusted sign flips, which is not observed.

Soft-mass contrasts for landmarks 00-09 change sign and rate within the window, so a time-conditioned contrast rule is more faithful than a constant rule. The hypothesis remains descriptive because the curves are contrasts, not absolute targets, and no validated fit establishes causal benefit.

The turnover residual is large and significant for several landmark features while the population rate is null, which is consistent with changing cohort composition or score reclassification rather than within-path change. A discriminating test would compare the residual against a decoded terminal label, which is unavailable in this study.

Shape_yy is the only shape component with a consistent negative sign across raw and adjusted correlation and full batch agreement, while shape_xx and shape_zz are weaker. A testable intervention would target shape_yy while leaving shape_xx and shape_zz free; the failure condition is a batch with opposite sign, not present in the supplied 14 batches.

Selection innovation is positively associated with teacher innovation-contrast alignment but negatively associated with observed child score gain, and teacher contrast is predominantly internal. This suggests that coherent joint patterns, not isolated marginal descriptors, express the reproducible coupling; the hypothesis remains descriptive because the association is within-selector and batch is the independent unit.

limitations: Decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable, so last-record joint-head credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.
Survival credit is recorded joint-head credit with thin ancestral coverage (349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors, 531 with fewer than 6) and only 14 complete-survival batches.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling, and is an accounting diagnostic rather than a causal selection effect.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals, and no adjustment beyond the supplied tool is claimed.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis are used.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.
All weak and null scalar effects are retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
The executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term, so moment and pair-kernel effects are diagnostic evidence only.
